name: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd
title: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd - 532899 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 268 cr from Rs 297 cr-ish... no—H1 revenue Rs 1,040 cr vs Rs 1,180 cr; cotton volumes fell, illegal BT cotton and inventory build weigh on margins, with cash about Rs 125 cr versus Rs 300 cr guided.

guidance.metric: Cash on books at Q2 end
guidance.value: Rs 125 cr (reported); guidance was close to Rs 300 cr

summary.headline: Kaveri Seed Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29.84% to Rs 1,040 crore (Rs 1,040.44 cr) with EBITDA margin 30.48%, net profit Rs 96.61 cr...
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 1,040.44 crore, up 29.84% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 315.88 crore at a 30.48% margin and net profit of Rs 96.61 crore (versus a Rs 6.47 crore loss a year earlier for net loss narrowing reference in the call). Standalone Q2 revenue was Rs 286.68 crore (about 13.32% decline) per the call's segment figures, with cotton revenue down 12.12% and non-cotton revenue up 29%; the transcript's figures are internally inconsistent in places and should be verified against the filing. Maize was the largest drag: revenue fell about 36.3% in the first half, partly due to a monsoon-related sowing shortfall and delayed onset, while non-cotton products grew with new hybrids in vegetables and rice. Management said cotton volume pressure is tied to illegal Bt cotton seed sales and that the company is shifting toward new hybrid cotton products, with 85-90% of the cotton portfolio expected to come from new hybrids over 3-4 years. Management flagged elevated maize and rice inventory (Rs 150 crore plus higher than last year) and higher cash-to-payables timing effects, and said export expansion into Bangladesh, Philippines, Indonesia, Tanzania and others is aimed at building its own brand.

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: Standalone cotton revenue of Rs 188.47 crore in Q2, down 12.12%, with management attributing the decline to illegal Bt cotton seed sales and a shift to new hybrid cotton portfolios.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Maize revenue fell 36.3% YoY in Q2 to Rs 22.37 crore; first-half maize sales were down about 30%, largely due to a poor monsoon and delayed onset in key states.

segments.name: Non-cotton (vegetables, rice, others)
segments.commentary: Non-cotton revenue grew 29% in Q2 to Rs 264.4 crore; vegetables revenue rose to Rs 70.56 crore (up 71.6%) and hybrid rice contributed Rs 169.45 crore for the quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export business grew from Rs 10-12 crore earlier to about Rs 65-70 crore currently per Q&A, with new country registrations in progress across 8 countries.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (Aditya Agritech, Kaveri Microtech, Kaveri Genomics)
segments.commentary: Management said Aditya Agritech had revenue of about Rs 100 crore plus and Kaveri Genomics roughly Rs 80 crore; the other two subsidiaries together contributed about Rs 100 crore or less of profit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the second half to be a lean period in northern cotton and maize seed; cotton sales for H2 are described as weaker.
Management said it is 'not worried' about inventory write-offs and expects the Rs 150 crore-plus inventory build to be used in Rabi and the next Kharif.
Consolidated EBITDA margin for H2 is guided at around 30% plus or minus 1-2%, with management saying margins for the full year should remain close to last year's levels.
Maize Kharif outlook is positive with acreage expected to grow; management said it is seeing good response and sentiment for next Kharif.
Management targets increasing its own-brand presence in export markets over the next 4-5 years, with registration timelines of 6-8 months per product and 3-4 years to establish brands.
capex_capacity: Capital work in progress is around Rs 120-130 crore, mainly land purchases and machinery; agricultural land being acquired is about 50-60% of the amount, with the remainder office/plant and machinery.
Management noted the inventory of seed has a usable life of 1.5-3 years for maize and 3-5 years for cotton, with rice and other varieties stored under controlled conditions.
Board approved an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share and the incorporation of a wholly-owned subsidiary in an overseas market (Philippines/Indonesia/Zambia/Peru context from the call).
demand_pricing: Maize prices were described as high at around Rs 2,500-3,000 per quintal in the call; management said maize is commodity-price sensitive and sales depend on monsoon timing.
Management said illegal GM cotton seed sales are eroding Kaveri's cotton market share, with the government reportedly taking steps against it.

Competitive set in cotton includes Bayer, Mahyco-type players and smaller local players; management said Kaveri competes on the new hybrid offerings across states including Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Dealer and distributor channel concentration: a few hybrid-linked products (468, 90, 8 hybrids) account for high volumes; management said the channel strategy remains intact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the thought process behind export expansion and the timeline to build own brands in Bangladesh, Philippines and Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports were around Rs 65-70 crore currently versus Rs 10-12 crore earlier; the model is to sell via distributors first, then register and build own-brand presence over 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cotton market share falling, and how is the company responding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to illegal Bt cotton seed sales; it is pursuing registration of new GM technologies, and new hybrids are expected to form 85-90% of the cotton portfolio over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory situation and write-off risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inventory built up by about Rs 150 crore versus last year, mainly rice and maize; it said there is no material write-off risk and that inventory will be used in Rabi and next Kharif.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin expectations for H2 and the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided H2 consolidated EBITDA margin at around 30% plus or minus 1-2%, with standalone margins down about 200 bps; full-year margins expected close to last year's levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the cash figure look low, and what is the consolidation effect of returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash fell due to the inventory build-up and payment timing; it said the returns relate to a liquidation effect and that the H1 comparison is affected by a consolidation timing effect.

risks_watch: Illegal Bt cotton seed sales continue to erode cotton market share, and management says the government is taking steps against them.
Inventory of about Rs 150 crore-plus above last year's level, with write-off risk on maize and rice if sales slow.
Weak H2 outlook for northern cotton and maize seed, with cyclone impact in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and rainfall variability.
Cash balance decline and receivables/payables timing; the call's cash figures and the subsidiary/standalone revenue split are inconsistent and need verification.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the quarter's consolidated growth and the new-hybrid pipeline, but cautious on cotton market share, inventory and the H2 outlook for cotton and maize. Several answers were hedged, with a few figures given approximately and some pending confirmation.

growth.why: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 29.84% YoY to Rs 1,040.44 cr, but the brief's standalone figures conflict (standalone revenue -13.32%, cotton -12.12%), and no revenue or EBITDA guidance percentage was given; H2 is guided as a lean period for cotton and maize with EBITDA margin around 30% plus or minus 1-2%, with no capacity additions or firm order backing cited.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H2 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 30% plus or minus 1-2% versus 30.48% in Q2, with full-year margin close to last year; standalone margin down about 190-200 bps, so no clear expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning was named; capital work in progress of Rs 120-130 crore is mainly land and machinery with no commissioning date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Non-cotton revenue grew 29% to Rs 264.4 crore and exports rose to about Rs 65-70 crore from Rs 10-12 crore, but cotton fell 12.12% to Rs 188.47 crore and H2 is a lean period for cotton and maize.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Cash fell to about Rs 125 crore from Rs 267 crore a year earlier, and no new capex plan was stated beyond the existing Rs 120-130 crore CWIP.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided H2 margin at around 30% plus or minus 1-2% and described H2 cotton and maize as weaker, with no revenue upgrade cited.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cotton volume pressure from illegal Bt seed sales, a weak H2 for northern cotton and maize, and cash guidance cut from about Rs 300 crore to Rs 125 crore raise downgrade risk, though the brief's figures are unverified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New hybrids in vegetables and rice are driving growth (vegetables up 71.6% to Rs 70.56 crore) and 85-90% of cotton portfolio is to come from new hybrids over 3-4 years, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Maize Kharif acreage and demand
rows.why: Management said Maize Kharif outlook is positive with acreage expected to grow and good response for next Kharif, after maize revenue fell 36.3% to Rs 22.37 crore in Q2.

rows.label: Rs 150 crore-plus inventory drawdown
rows.why: Management expects the Rs 150 crore-plus inventory build (mainly rice and maize) to be used in Rabi and next Kharif, though cash fell to Rs 125 crore from Rs 267 crore a year earlier.

rows.label: Export own-brand build-out
rows.why: Exports grew to about Rs 65-70 crore from Rs 10-12 crore with new registrations in progress across 8 countries, with 6-8 months per product registration and 3-4 years to build brands.

tone.note: Management was confident on consolidated growth, non-cotton hybrids and exports, but cautious on cotton share loss to illegal Bt seed, inventory and the weak H2 for cotton and maize; analysts pressed on cash, inventory and figure inconsistencies.
